parameters.title: Reproduce the bug
parameters.instructions:
Write a regression test under ${test_path} that reproduces the reported bug through the code's public
behaviour. Run ${test_cmd} and confirm the new test fails for the reason the bug describes, not because of a
typo or a missing import. Do not touch ${src_path} in this step.

parameters.title: Fix the root cause
Explain the fix
parameters.instructions:
Write ${notes_dir}/bugfix.md for the reviewer with three short sections: "## Cause" (what was wrong and why it
happened), "## Fix" (what changed and why it is the smallest correct change) and "## Proof" (which test
reproduces it and what it asserts).

nodeGroups.name: Fix with proof
nodeGroups.description:
You are fixing one reported bug. Work in three moves and never skip ahead: first prove the bug exists with a test
that fails, then change the code until that test passes, then write down what was wrong. A fix without a failing
test first is a guess. Keep the change as small as the root cause allows; do not refactor or tidy unrelated code.

macros.title: Fix with proof
macros.instructions:
You are fixing one reported bug. Work in three moves and never skip ahead: first prove the bug exists with a test
that fails, then change the code until that test passes, then write down what was wrong. A fix without a failing
test first is a guess. Keep the change as small as the root cause allows; do not refactor or tidy unrelated code.

work_packages.title: Reproduce the bug
work_packages.instructions:
Write a regression test under ${test_path} that reproduces the reported bug through the code's public
behaviour. Run ${test_cmd} and confirm the new test fails for the reason the bug describes, not because of a
typo or a missing import. Do not touch ${src_path} in this step.

checklist.assert: a test file under the test paths was added or changed
checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${test_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${test_path} | grep -q .

checklist.assert: the test suite fails, so the new test reproduces the bug

checklist.judge: Does this change add a test that exercises the reported bug through public behaviour and asserts the correct result? FAIL if the test would also fail for an unrelated reason (a typo, a missing import, a wrong fixture), if it asserts the buggy behaviour, or if the change also edits source code.

work_packages.title: Fix the root cause

checklist.cmd: git diff --name-only ${base_ref} -- ${src_path} | grep -q . || git ls-files --others --exclude-standard -- ${src_path} | grep -q .

checklist.assert: no test file was deleted to get to green

checklist.judge: Does this change fix the cause of the bug rather than its symptom? FAIL if it special-cases the test's input, swallows or hides an error, weakens, skips or deletes a test, or changes behaviour the bug report did not ask to change.

work_packages.title: Explain the fix
work_packages.instructions:
Write ${notes_dir}/bugfix.md for the reviewer with three short sections: "## Cause" (what was wrong and why it
happened), "## Fix" (what changed and why it is the smallest correct change) and "## Proof" (which test
reproduces it and what it asserts).

checklist.assert: the note has Cause, Fix and Proof sections
checklist.cmd: for section in Cause Fix Proof; do grep -q "^## $section" ${notes_dir}/bugfix.md || exit 1; done

checklist.assert: the note carries at least 60 words

checklist.judge: Does this note name the actual cause of the bug, the change that fixed it and the test that proves it, in terms a reviewer can check against the code? FAIL if it is generic, if it claims something the code does not show, or if the proof does not name a test.
